summary: Hans Kamstrup Vogt was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Universities of Oslo, Paris, and Yale, earning his Ph.D. in Oslo and training under Antoine Meillet and Edward Sapir, later serving as Professor of General Linguistics at Oslo (1946–1973).
Hans Karl Siegert was a linguist who studied at the University of Munich under Walther Wüst.
Hans Krahe was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Ferdinand Sommer and Friedrich Karl Slotty. He held posts at Jena, Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen.

Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and Institut Catholique de Paris before serving on the faculty at the University of Tübingen from around 1960 to 1996.

Hans Losch was an Indologist who studied at Munich and the University of Bonn, earning a law degree and a Ph.D. under Hermann Jacobi and Willibald Kirfel. He spent his academic career at Bonn as a Privatdozent, professor, Diätendozent, and wissenschaftlicher Rat.

Hans Much was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the Universities of Marburg, Kiel, and Berlin, earned his Dr.med. at the University of Würzburg, and became Professor of Medicine at the University of Hamburg in 1919.

Hans Nordewin von Körber worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Bonn, Cambridge, and Marburg, where he received his Ph.D., and served as Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Southern California (~1929–1961).

Hans Reichelt was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Vienna and Giessen under Georg Bühler, Christian Bartholomae, and others, later holding posts at Chernivtsi, Graz (rector), Hamburg, and Innsbruck.

Hans Schacht worked in Indology and linguistics. After earning his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin, he taught at secondary schools in Lausanne and served as Privatdozent of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne from 1903 to 1933.

Hans T. Bakker is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held posts at Utrecht University and the University of Groningen (~1988–2013), and served as a curator at the British Museum.
Hans Urs von Balthasar was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Zurich from around 1923 to 1928, including under Bernhard Geiger.
Hans West was an Indologist who studied at Odense Katedralskole (~1774–1777) and served as rector at the Danish School in Christiansted in 1788.

Hans Wilhelm Haussig was a historian of Iranian, Central Asian, and Near Eastern history. After studying under Robert Bleichsteiner and earning his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin, he held professorships at the Free University of Berlin and Ruhr University Bochum.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar who held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1926–1929), and Kiel University (~1929–1935).

Hans Wirtz worked in Indology and Sinology. He studied at Berlin, Munich, and Bonn, completing his Ph.D. under Hermann Jacobi, and later served as a teacher at the University of Cologne from 1922 to 1929.

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Augustana, Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp, Bonn under Gustav Mensching, and Harvard, later serving as Director at the University of Bonn.
Hans-Joachim Rassat was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen between ~1950 and 1955, studying under Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Hans-Rudolf Kantor works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Delhi, National Taiwan University, and Bonn, and has held faculty posts at Huafan University, Tamkang University, Fo Guang Shan, Fo Guang University, and National Chengchi University.
Hans-Ulrich Rieker was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. A disciple of Anagarika Govinda, he founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala in 1952 and served as its leader until approximately 1964.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indologist who studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt.
